incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: elevated 5xx rate detected for inference-gateway-private-1 (customer: AcmeCorp). 504/502 spike starting ~2638001200. Paging oncall @Maria (oncall rota).
Maria (oncall): grabbing it. looking at dashboards now — seeing spike across two AZs. Client errors concentrated on 'private-1' peered VPCs. ETA 2m.
Maria (oncall): top-line: 504s from gateway -> backend inference pods timing out, connection resets also showing from upstream NAT/transit appliance. QPS stable but error rate jumped from 0.2% to 18%.
Maria (oncall): curl to gateway returns 504 intermittently. logs show backend connections closed with RST after ~1s.
Devon (net): @Maria do we have any recent firewall/egress policy rollouts for private-*? I see an automation job completed ~20m ago (fw-rule-sync v3.4).
Maria (oncall): checking ops-runbook and recent deploys... yes, firewall rule sync v3.4 rolled at 2638000000 targeting transit-fw in private region. Could be related.
Devon (net): pulling conntrack and nat stats from transit appliance (private transit-01):

```
# show conntrack summary
conntrack: 524k entries, 95% used
# iptables -t nat -L -n --line-numbers
Chain POSTROUTING (policy ACCEPT)
num  target     prot opt source               destination         
1    SNAT       tcp  --  10.0.0.0/16          0.0.0.0/0           to:54.211.11.30:32768-61000
```

Devon (net): nat range looks normal but conntrack churn is high. also seeing lots of SYN->RST from transit-fw. pulling firewall rules now.
Devon (net): firewall rule v3.4 includes a line that rewrites ephemeral NAT range and also a deny rule for ephemeral ports to a set of ASN IPs: `-m multiport --dports 32768:61000 -j DROP` — that looks wrong. automation applied a drop for ephemeral egress to a CIDR set used by partner peering.
Maria (oncall): that would explain return packets being dropped for established connections — asymmetry: SNAT to ephemeral port, but return hit DROP so backend times out -> 504s. Can you confirm which peered CIDR set matched?
Devon (net): matched prefix list `peering-partner-blocklist-2026-03` containing customer peer ranges. Somebody accidentally inverted the rule when templating. I can also see flow logs showing TCP syn/ack accepted but subsequent client packets getting RST/ICMP from transit-fw.
Jamie (CS): AcmeCorp is getting a spike in errors on their production tenant — they just pinged support. We should push an OOB notice if mitigation >10m. Can we do a quick mitigation now?
Maria (oncall): mitigation options: 1) revert firewall rule v3.4 (fast but requires safe rollout check) 2) add explicit allow for ephemeral ports to AcmeCorp peering CIDRs 3) BGP route tweak to force symmetric return path to avoid transit-fw.
Linus (infra): I can stage an immediate rollback of the fw-sync job (v3.3) to all transit nodes in region. Rollback will apply in ~45s per node, total ~3m. Reverting seems lowest risk.
Maria (oncall): do it. also flip on model-fallback and increase health-check timeout for the affected gateway to reduce customer visible 504s — we can route some traffic to backup pool.
Linus (infra): rollback started. running: `fw-sync rollback --job fw-sync:v3.4 --to v3.3 --region private-eu` — progress 1/4 nodes done.
SRE Bot: Deploy rollback job accepted (id: rollback-99871). Notifying oncall.
Maria (oncall): applying temporary routing fix on LB: set backend healthcheck timeout -> 10s, and mark canary fallback route enabled for AcmeCorp route: `route-policy acmecorp -> fallback-pool`.
Maria (oncall): also enabling prefix exception to allow 32768:61000 for peer CIDR 10.64.0.0/16 while rollback completes: `fwctl add-allow --src 10.64.0.0/16 --dports 32768:61000` — applying now.
Devon (net): I pushed the temporary allow on transit-fw instances; flows show ephemeral ports now moving again. conntrack usage stabilizing — entries dropping from 95% -> 70%.
Linus (infra): rollback completed on 3/4 nodes, final node finishing — should be fully reverted in 90s.
Maria (oncall): monitoring logs... error rate dropping from 18% -> 3% over the last 2 minutes. customer symptoms reduced, spikes still occasional.
Jamie (CS): informing AcmeCorp: short note: "We're mitigating an infrastructure egress rule issue affecting some private inference requests. We've applied a fix and are monitoring — expect recovery within minutes. Follow-up postmortem to be shared." Should I send now or after stable 10m?
Maria (oncall): send now as a proactive update. include ETA 30m for full verification and potential additional follow-up.
Jamie (CS): sent to AcmeCorp: "We're seeing reduced errors after a mitigation. Engineering rolled back a recent firewall sync and added a temporary allow for your peering range. We're monitoring and will follow up with a detailed root cause and timeline."
Devon (net): confirming full traffic path: traceroutes show symmetric path now. `tcptraceroute` results to backend show no more RSTs. TCP metrics: retransmit rate back to baseline.
Maria (oncall): marking incident as 'mitigating' and moving to oncall handoff in 20m. Linus, can you take next 2h primary for validation and postmortem draft? I'll create the incident ticket and capture timelines.
Linus (infra): I got it. I'll collect firewall diffs, automation template, and the change that inverted match logic. Will start P1 postmortem doc and include remediation: add unit test to fw-sync so ephemeral ranges can't be blackholed, and require a human review for rule inversions.
SRE Bot: Incident status updated: MITIGATING -> Acknowledged, assignee Linus (infra).
Maria (oncall): final check: error rate now 0.4% and trending to baseline. I'll sign out. Thanks team.
Linus (infra): will keep monitoring, will post full RCA and customer timeline by EOD. Adding action items: rollback review, automation fix, improved runbook for quick allow vs rollback decision.
Jamie (CS): I coordinated with AcmeCorp support, asked for any logs they have; they confirmed fewer errors. will keep them notified.
incident-bot: Note: create postmortem ticket and tag incident-ops, net-eng, cs.autoresponder
Maria (oncall): :white_check_mark: handoff complete. leaving channel.
